items.body: Review by KansasForEver4 — A band with a Tennessee vibe? Well, yes, because EVERSHIP hails from Nashville, a city better known for rock 'n' roll and bananas than for progressive rock! Yet it's from there that Shane Atkinson decided to send us his flagship album. Shane is a multi-instrumentalist composer who worked as a studio musician in the eighties and nineties, even composing commercials and film scores to make ends meet. After dabbling in the software industry, music haunted him so much that he decided to return to it, starting in 2005 with his own recording studio and equipment. The first compositions for the album presented here date back to 2009, so seven solid years to arrive at the remarkable result of this self-titled debut album.hane Atkinson handled almost all the instruments, with a few guest musicians including his own brother James on acoustic and lead guitars, and the invaluable vocal contribution of Beau West, an old childhood friend. And what vocals they are! From the very first track, "Silver Light," Freddie must be turning in his grave, so strongly does the song's emphasis evoke Queen, so powerfully operatic?an influence claimed (among others) by the master of ceremonies himself, the Queen of the pre-"News of the World" era, the very rock, frenetic Queen of the first five albums. The second track, "A Slow Descent Into Reality," takes us back to Liverpool in 1970 (and even earlier?), so strong is the influence of the Merseyside quartet in the opening. This is further enhanced by Queen's operatic feel, a touch of Kansas from Nicelle Priebe's violin, and a dash of classic Yes (the intricate bass lines and enchanting backing vocals). In short, a veritable who's who of the genre, all showcased by Shane Atkinson's multifaceted talent.And what can be said about the splendid "Evermore" that follows? Calm, delicate, and melodic (both divine and lyrical), with a magical piano, the electric guitar takes on a Bostonian character (though recapturing Tom Scholz's distinctive sound is no easy feat), and, as always, those majestic and magnificent backing vocals?a truly great moment of progressive rock. "Ultima Thule" continues in the same vein, a clear vocal tribute to our dearly departed Freddie and Brad in particular. Beau West establishes himself as an undeniable heir with his shimmering and delicate timbre, all sprinkled with a sublime violin in the finale. It's beautiful, it's wonderful...We thought we'd heard it all, but no! "Flying Machine" nails us to the delightful pillory of timeless progressive music. Our bliss and delight are unparalleled. The choirs, always the choirs (again, Boston, and also the entire musical spectrum of melodic rock from the last thirty years, not forgetting, on the other side of the Atlantic, the ever-popular Moody Blues), flood this track from beginning to end, and the orchestrations are simply fabulous.One minor point, but one that only concerns your reviewer: I didn't recognize the Theremin and Dulcimer that are supposed to be on the album. And a small criticism of this work: there's a lot of singing, but it's so well sung that forgiveness is in order.Another contender for the podium, a podium for which three steps won't be enough this year.Simply magnificent.Thank you, Mr. Atkinson.

items.body: Review by alainPP — 35 Tapes, sounds of the 70s, Genesis, Camel, and King Crimson. The studio band uses the 35 tapes as a reference point in the Mellotron, combining them with symphonic neo-prog."Hallway" is vintage pop-rock on period keyboards, hinting at the Crimson sound with its ethereal guitars. The rapid variation on the wooden piano evokes a solemn memory, the marshmallow guitar amplifying the meditative, nostalgic atmosphere. "Water" features languid Crimson-esque keyboards, Hackett-like guitar, a somber, melancholic air with hushed vocals, and a prominent bass reminiscent of Genesis's second era. The melting pot transforms into a musical axolotl, suspended between two worlds, with a melancholic finale. "Brise" combines soft keyboards and languid, contemplative vocal harmonies. The sound recalls Rick Miller's work with Hackett-style guitar, focusing on his psychic self etched in the mirror. A fusion of delicate, ever-evolving pop-rock sounds, a melancholic instrumental drift?the key word for this album. An ethereal, Genesis-esque, nostalgic, radiant finale."Borrowed Time" features a prominent bassline of symphonic prog rock, tearful and emotionally charged. The distant acoustic Greek guitar melody evokes the intense, charismatic atmosphere of Genesis, a magnified ersatz. A plaintive final guitar solo melts the listener's heart. "Clueless" is pop-rock with a rich vocal and a catchy, yet not over-the-top, rhythm. A touch of Canterbury lends itself to this meandering, timeless journey, allowing you to savor this vintage, cinematic moment. "Cities" opens with a melting, marshmallow-like guitar solo, a nostalgic beauty. The compressed melancholy recalls the aura of King Crimson, with vocals reminiscent of John. A shimmering piece poised between sadness and hope, the mystery of its composition blends numerous references to the 70s. The contained explosion, bass and organ intertwined for the keyboard finale on "Burning Rope," is fresh and joyful, filling the atmosphere with its energy.35 Tapes offers an immersion into misty realms where reality and imagination merge. Expect introspection, Mellotron, emotion, gentleness, and warmth.

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — With members from bands I've already reviewed (Raccomandata Ricevuta Ritorno, Teoremi, and L'Uovo Di Colombo), Samadhi worked similarly to Il Volo, being a supergroup that leaned to the more pop aspects of Rock Progressivo Italiano. At only thirty five minutes long, I can definitely see room for improvement, but overall, a fine record that captures that more charming aspects of Italian prog at the time. It has a symphonic twinge that works well with the nature of the group, and though it can feel a little lackluster or uninspired, I can see a strong vision that came out as an okay project. The front cover also could've been more interesting other than just the simplistic design it holds. Moving on, among the players of the band, I overall enjoyed Luciano Regoli's vocals the most, as they fit the warm atmosphere of the music. The majority of the songs are all quite short, only being a few minutes long, but each of them has a nice whimsy to it that fills the area with a fun spirit. One thing I thought could've had more work was the production, as it feels a too hazy and it can come off as a little weak at points. My favorites from this album were the joyous and energized opener of Uomo Stanco, the quirky and sweet sound of L'Angelo, the cooler jam band vibes of Passaggio Di Via Arpino, and the longer more classically influenced L'Ultima Spiaggia, which also closes the record. On this album I could hear elements of what would later form into the sound of Maxophone, having that playful yet secretly quite intricate sound. On here, however, it can come off as feeling pretentious or that the band thinks they're doing something much more grand and greater than it actually is. Sure, it's good music with some pretty good high points here and there, but I wouldn't say it's life changing or anything. In conclusion, Samadhi is essentially just your run-of-the-mill Rock Progressivo Italiano record. Nothing mind-blowing, just some good tunes with some fine details sprinkled in. I'm thinking a strong 3.25/5 or a light 3.5/5 for this one.

items.body: Athens duo Incirrina have released the album “Trace” on the German label Cold Transmission Music. The Incirrina “Trace” album runs to 11 tracks and follows the duo’s two previous albums, “8.15” (2019) and “Lip Led Scream” (2022). The band describe “Trace” as built around freedom, identity and resistance. The 11 tracks were written between 2023 and 2025 and recorded through a 24-channel console, using analogue electronic instruments and the duo’s vocals. The album follows “Lip Led Scream” (2022), the duo’s first record for Cold Transmission Music. “Trace” is issued on vinyl (black and crystal-clear), CD, a limited cassette and digital. “Mutate” and “Always Here” were released as advance singles, and “Mutate” has an accompanying video on YouTube. The album is available through Cold Transmission Music (coldtransmission.com) and the band’s Bandcamp. Trace by Incirrina About Incirrina Incirrina is a dark electronic and minimal synth duo based in Athens, Greece, formed in late 2017 by George Katsanos (synthesizers, drum machine, waterphone, vocals) and Irini Tiniakou (synthesizers, vocals). The duo describe their work as “dark, poetic, electronic,” pairing analogue synth lines and drum-machine rhythms with Tiniakou’s vocals. Tiniakou first appeared as a guest vocalist on a release by the Greek act Metal Disco before Incirrina became a project in its own right. The duo debuted with the album “8.15” (2019, Geheimnis Records), a record drawing on the work of the 18th-century poet William Blake. They followed it with the digital maxi-single “Utter” (2020) and a 2021 split maxi-single with The Man & His Failures, “Devastations / R.Daneel,” on Smash Records. Their second album, “Lip Led Scream” (2022), was their first release for Germany’s Cold Transmission Music, which has handled their releases since. In 2024 they released the double single “Immersion” (“Presence” and “Alien Room”), also on Cold Transmission Music. In an April 2023 Side-Line reviewer Inferno Sound Diaries described “Lip Led Scream” as “a pure Cold-Wave production which is sometimes reinforced with harder, EBM, elements” and as “a well-crafted and fully enjoyable work without any single cut to throw away,” rating it 8/10. The duo have performed in Greece, Germany, Belgium, Hungary and Croatia, with festival appearances at Plíísken Festival, Morphic Festival, Cold Transmission Festival. Death Disco Festival – The Warm Up, Athens Music Week, Metavasis Festival and the Athens Digital Arts Festival. “Trace,” their third album, is their latest release for Cold Transmission Music.

items.body: Steve Roach‘s “Quiet Music” series, originally recorded between 1983 and 1986 and released on Projekt Records, will be available on vinyl for the first time as a complete 3LP set. The Steve Roach “Quiet Music” 40th Anniversary edition is pressed on three ultra clear 140g LPs in a limited edition of 300 copies, and will be out August 7, 2026 so Audioglobe informs. The set collects all three original “Quiet Music” albums in one outer sleeve with black paper inner sleeves and a two-sided credits insert. The pressing is 140g ultra clear vinyl, limited strictly to 300 copies. The full tracklist across the three LPs is as follows. “Quiet Music 1”: A1 “The Green Place, Part I” (24:44); B1 “The Green Place, Part II” (24:52). “Quiet Music 2”: A1 “See Things” (5:45); A2 “Towards the Blue” (3:20); A3 “Something in Tears” (5:18); A4 “A Few More Moments” (13:05); B1 “Air and Light” (25:51). “Quiet Music 3”: A1 “Dreaming and Sleep” (18:16); A2 “Quiet Canon” (7:28); B1 “Sleep and Dreaming” (24:47). Quiet Music by Steve Roach Here’s what Steve Roach says on “Quiet Music” at 40 years: “In looking at the arc of my music, 40 years after creating Quiet Music,” Roach stated in the release materials, “I still feel an unbroken connection to this same inner breath and pulse I was discovering within myself and my creative life at that time. Even with everything that was going on in the early ’80s — musically, culturally, politically — this music came to exist in its own dimension, outside of that time, separate from the day-to-day climate in which I was surrounded. I was yearning to express a timeless and universal soul-tone, a safe haven within the music.” Composer Harold Budd said this when the release first came out in 1986: “I think Steve Roach’s Quiet Music is his best album. It’s not that it’s simply pretty (which it is), but there’s an odd edge lurking in the background that moves it miles away from ‘New Age’ torpor. This is a lovely album from a composer working at the top of his skills.” About Steve Roach Steve Roach is an American composer and performer born in 1955, based in Tucson, Arizona. He began working with synthesizers in the early 1980s and established an international reputation through recordings released on Projekt Records, among other labels. His 1984 album “Structures from Silence” – reissued on its third vinyl edition by Projekt in April 2025 – is considered a foundational work of ambient music. The “Quiet Music” series originated in commissions for healing-arts programmes and was released on cassette in 1986; the recordings draw on synthesizers, flute, electric piano and natural sounds. Roach has continued releasing new studio and live work at high frequency; Our most recent coverage concerned the limited 2CD live release “La Rosa — Live in Tucson, 2025” in May 2026. The “Quiet Music” 3LP set, out August 7, 2026, marks the first time the complete series has been issued on vinyl in a single edition.

items.body: Norwegian solo artist Chris Wicked releases a gothic rock and dark synthpop cover of Depeche Mode‘s “Enjoy the Silence” on June 2, 2026, via Raven Black Productions. The Bergen-based artist here mixes gothic, cinematic and alternative rock. This is the third single from his forthcoming EP “Black Horns & Black Hooves.” Chris Wicked explains his reasons for choosing the song: “Enjoy the Silence has always been a song that resonated with me. The atmosphere, the sense of longing and the timeless darkness within the melody have inspired me since I was young. We didn’t want to copy the original — we wanted to reinterpret it through our own musical universe.” The cover arrives as the third single from the upcoming EP “Black Horns & Black Hooves” on Raven Black Productions. It follows “Utan Dina Andetag,” a cover of a Kent track released in December 2024 as the first single from the project, and “Wicked Game,” a cover of the Chris Isaak song released in September 2025 as the second single. About Chris Wicked Chris Wicked is a solo artist from Bergen, Norway. He came to wider attention as the founder and vocalist of Malice In Wonderland, a Norwegian rock band formed in the late 1990s before releasing a debut album and single “Lucifer’s Town” in 2005. Musically Malice In Wonderland’s sound combines glam, goth and hard rock elements. The band toured across Europe and Asia, sharing stages with acts including Def Leppard, and appeared in television productions. Their final album, “The Royal Brigade,” was released in December 2013, mixed by John Fryer, known for his work with Depeche Mode and Nine Inch Nails. In August 2015, Malice In Wonderland announced their break-up and completed a series of farewell shows in Norway and abroad. Chris Wicked subsequently announced a solo career, recording under his own name. His debut solo album, “Aleine,” was released in 2021 via Apollon Records and featured guest appearances from Gaahl (Gorgoroth), Hoest (Taake), Niklas Kvarforth (Shining) and V’gandr (Helheim). In 2024, he released the dark Nordic folk single “Northern Heart” on Raven Black Productions. Malice In Wonderland returned in 2025 to mark the 20th anniversary of their 2005 debut, releasing new and reimagined material including “I’ve Chosen Darkness (Over You)” and a revisited edition of “Lucifer’s Town” in 2025, followed by the single “Dying Breed” in 2026.

Side A: “Venerated & Despised” (2:34), “A Black Egg” (3:54), “Castrate Christ” (4:37), “Liken Ingen Jord Vill Svälja” (2:34), “Alone/A/Cross/Abyss” (3:48). Side B: “Thirty-Nine Lashes” (2:37), “The Seventh Man” (3:24), “Konung Krönt I Blod” (3:30), “A Ceaseless Howling” (3:29), “He Who Is My Mirror” (5:17). Perfection & Permanence by Trepaneringsritualen About Trepaneringsritualen Trepaneringsritualen is a death industrial and ritual ambient project founded by Swedish artist Thomas Martin Ekelund in 2008, initially based in Göteborg, Sweden, and later relocating to Berlin, Germany. The project released its first full-length, “Deathward, to the Womb”, in 2012 on Cold Spring Records. Side-Line reviewed the album at the time of release. “Perfection & Permanence” followed in 2014 on the same label, issued simultaneously on CD and LP; the white vinyl LP edition was limited to 500 copies. In 2017, Trepaneringsritualen released the full-length “Kainskult” on Tesco Organisation, and the project also collaborated with MZ.412 on the live document “Post Industriale / Rituals” 2LP. The same year, the project compiled two earlier split LPs on the CD “Yours Is a Kingdom of Death”. In 2018, Trepaneringsritualen and Nordvargr released “Alpha Ænigma”, a collaborative album. The project subsequently appeared on Cold Spring’s compilation “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” in 2023. In 2021, Thomas Martin Ekelund partnered with Henrik Nordvargr Björkk on “Lidaverken Del I: Att i Vådeld Förgås”. The project has released further albums including “ᛉᛦ – Algir; eller Algir i Merkstave” (2019) and “The Totality of Death (A)” and “The Totality of Death (Ω)” (both 2024). The repress of Trepaneringsritualen “Perfection & Permanence” is available via Cold Spring Records.

items.body: Denver project Neo Dimes has released “Alone,” a ten-track debut full-length album spanning darkwave, neo-industrial, alternative rock and synthpop. The album arrived on vinyl and cassette on May 19, 2026, with the digital release scheduled later this month later. Neo Dimes is the solo project of Denver-based musician Stephen Edmunds. “Alone” addresses digital-age isolation, algorithmic control, surveillance capitalism, online extremism and the experience of aging into a world shaped by technology. The record mixes neo-industrial, alternative rock, darkwave and synthpop. Alone by Neo Dimes The album’s artwork is built around a visual narrative: each of the ten single covers functions as a chapter, representing themes of paranoia, persuasion, control and acceptance, which combine to form the final album cover. Edmunds commented as follows on the album’s intent: “I recently lost a career right as my daughter came into the world — a world where she has fewer rights than her mother did and where tyranny is creeping into every facet of life. We’re addicted to the technology in our pockets that opens us to the world by consuming us entirely. It’s omnipresent and inescapable, and I’m pissed off.” Several tracks were released as singles ahead of the album. “Beasts” addresses what Edmunds describes as the radicalization of young men in the wake of the collapse of the American dream. “Angels” casts digital connectivity and surveillance as a modern substitute for guardianship. “Don’t Think” addresses manufactured consent and propaganda. “Trigger” connects personal experiences of addiction, anxiety and isolation. Note that a music video for “Trigger,” directed by Ty Borkowski, was also released. About Neo Dimes Neo Dimes is the solo project of Stephen Edmunds, a Denver, Colorado-based musician. Edmunds has spent most of his life as a musician, starting with guitar in hardcore and metal bands before moving into shoegaze and experimental music. The Neo Dimes project developed over approximately seven years, during which Edmunds worked through the production and compositional process largely through self-teaching. The project made its first public appearance in late 2024, when Edmunds contributed a remix of “Careful What You Wish For” by Highlands. The first original Neo Dimes material appeared in late 2025, with the single “Angels” released on October 30, 2025, followed by “Beasts” on December 9, 2025. Further singles, including “Don’t Think,” preceded the album’s release. Edmunds cites Nine Inch Nails, Depeche Mode and Deftones as primary influences, with The Cure, Joy Division, Brian Jonestown Massacre, My Bloody Valentine and The Prodigy also cited as formative references. “Alone” is the first full-length release under the Neo Dimes name.

items.body: French duo Potochkine‘s 2025 album “Sang d’Encre” is back in a second limited vinyl pressing on the young & cold label Audioglobe informs us. The new edition is limited to 333 copies on grey splatters vinyl. The first vinyl edition of “Sang d’Encre,” issued in late 2025, was pressed on red transparent with black marble vinyl. The current pressing uses grey splatters vinyl. Both pressings are limited to 333 copies. The album is also available on CD and digital. Sang d'Encre by POTOCHKINE “Sang d’Encre” holds seven tracks: “Bi,” “Endorphines,” “Partir,” “Tristesse Fantasmée,” “Bonnie,” “Pénurie de Larmes,” and the closing ambient piece “La Source.” Two tracks have accompanying videos: “Bi” and “Endorphines”. About Potochkine Potochkine is a French dark electronic duo formed in Paris in 2016, composed of vocalist Pauline Alcaïdé and producer Hugo Sempé. The pair built their sound around French-language vocals, electronic rhythms and a production approach drawing on EBM, electro and elements of darkwave and coldwave. The duo’s debut was the EP “Libérez votre imagination” (2016), which introduced their combination of dark electronics and theatrical staging. They followed with the self-titled album “Potochkine” (2018) and “Mythes” (2019), before releasing “Sortilèges” in 2021 on young & cold – their first release for the German label. A remix companion, “Sortilèges dans le club,” also appeared in 2021. The single “Endorphines” was released in 2024 ahead of “Sang d’Encre.” “Sang d’Encre” was released in autumn 2025 on young & cold as Potochkine’s fourth studio album and their second record for the label. The second vinyl pressing, on grey splatters vinyl, is available now through the young & cold webshop and its distribution network via Audioglobe.

items.body: Tomasz Lukowicz has already earned his stripes with his Fractal project, through which he has released a truckload of productions. With Replicant, he reveals another side of his skills, and on the debut album “Critical Point”, he delivers 11 compelling tracks. Replicant sounds very different — more like an experiment in which the operator takes us deep into his sonic laboratory, completely unleashing his creativity in sound design. He supports these experiments with slow rhythms and broken beats. Lukowicz reveals himself here as a true sound architect, showcasing an impressive sonic landscape. I particularly enjoy the depth he creates in his bass lines, as well as some of the space-like electro arrangements. The whole album remains entirely instrumental. A touch of vocals or sampling here and there would not have felt out of place, but “Critical Point” already stands firmly on its own. The album even contains a few minimalist gems that are simply impossible to ignore. This is the kind of release that would have appealed to fans of the Tympanik Audio label back in the day, but which has now found the right home on Aliens Production. Call it Experimental with a touch of IDM subtlety, or simply Electro freestyle — this debut album is certainly an intriguing discovery. (Rating:8). Listen to “Depressing Fate Of Humanity”: https://aliensproduction.bandcamp.com/track/depresing-fate-of-humanity

items.body: Puerta Negra’s latest single Complejo de Victima (Victim Mentality), comes on as a scathing indictment delivered with immaculate control. It’s strict, stylish, and wired for confrontation. Here, the Portland duo of María Aguirre and Mark Arciaga treat body music as a blunt instrument with a brain attached to it, and this lead single from their Metafísica EP sharpens the blade without polishing away any vitriol. Sung entirely in Spanish, the track places Aguirre’s voice at the center of the damage, cool and cutting, while the beat lurches forward with the mechanical confidence of a machine trained on human spite. Musically, Complejo de Victima works from a lean EBM chassis and lets the parts rattle. Industrial funk pressure runs through the track, but it never loosens into party decoration. The electronics have a mutant bite, closer to a feverish factory floor than a club fantasy, while the broken rhythms keep shoving the body forward at odd angles. Oráculo references Cabaret Voltaire, new-beat mutations, and the contemporary EBM revival, showcasing themselves as a band pushing their musical heritage through clenched teeth. Directed by Zach Flanary, the official video keeps its world deliberately stripped down: black-and-white, high contrast, bodies under pressure, faces treated less as glamour objects than as evidence. Aguirre and Arciaga perform as if trapped inside the song’s own nervous system, caught between command and collapse. The mirror shots give the video its mean little genius. They bend the performance into something fractured without dragging it into cheap psychodrama. A face splits, a figure doubles, the eye gets tricked into watching the watcher, and the victim complex named in the title starts to feel less like a diagnosis than a room full of bad faith. There is no need for plot when the premise is already poisoned: accusation, self-pity, control, and the private theater people build around their own wounds. Watch the video for Complejo de Victima below: Metafísica is billed as the third chapter in Puerta Negra’s vision, following 2022’s Costo Humano and 2023’s Playa Sola, and Complejo de Victima feels like a hard pivot toward austerity, attack, and psychic compression. Severity can be seductive when handled with nerve. Listen to Complejo de Victima below and pre-order the vinyl (out June 12th from Oráculo Records) here. items.body: In Anthology, the debut EP by Glaswork, Joshua Elijah makes a departure from the sharper angles of his previous work with Inertia Her, entering a more severe, spacious register. The Paris-based artist, producer, mixing engineer, and photographer has carried over a certain discipline from his earlier work, but the gesture here is one of subtraction rather than expansion. Across five tracks, Glaswork strips song form down to pressure, pulse, and pallor, allowing ambient electronics, contemporary classical texture, and EBM-derived movement to meet in a place where precision becomes emotional. The record has the feel of architecture abandoned before occupancy: corridors of tone, low mechanical thuds, rooms implied by resonance rather than filled with ornament. Elijah’s use of analogue and digital processes gives the music a tactile instability, as if each sound were being handled while still warm from the machine. There are traces of Tim Hecker’s engulfing grain and CoH’s sleek austerity, but Glaswork’s instincts are more private, less grandly apocalyptic. He works in measured gestures, allowing a bass figure or a softened industrial pulse to appear, recede, and leave behind a kind of charged absence. “Anthology is the result of mixing analogue and digital processes and letting experimentation lead the way,” says Elijah. “…five tracks built from dark electronic textures, ambient space, and restrained rhythmic ideas, focused more on mood and atmosphere than structure.” The statement points to the EP’s central temperament. These pieces do not hurry toward resolution. They collect and disperse, gathering weight through proximity. A rhythm may suggest the body, but it rarely gives itself over to club logic; a synth line may gesture toward melody, then dissolve into a colder field of tone. Elijah seems uninterested in spectacle, choosing instead to let small details carry the burden of feeling: the grain at the edge of a drone, the blunt knock of a beat, the way a suspended note can seem to alter the scale of the room around it. The EP’s emotional force lies in that refusal of excess. Glaswork begins here as a project of concentration, one concerned with the drama of reduction, where darkness is measured, space is active, and silence becomes another instrument in the arrangement. Listen to Anthology below and pre-order the album here. items.body: Re:Mission Entertainment has signed somemagicalshit, the bilingual synthpop and dark electronic project of Houston’s Courtnii Veronica Rose, with a debut full-length album set for release this fall. The announcement gives a proper label frame to a project already wired for bruised nerves, bad glamour, private panic, and the kind of synth damage that makes a bedroom feel like a pirate radio broadcast tower. Rose started somemagicalshit in 2022 as a solo operation: computer, synths, sequencers, and a skull full of voltage. By 2023, the project had grown into a full live band, which makes sense, because this is the kind of music that wants bodies dancing in front of it. It has Le Tigre’s art-damaged bite, TR/ST’s bruised electronic glamour, ADULT.’s stern machine-body snap, Pussy Riot’s bilingual agit-pop provocation, and the frostbitten drama of Kælan Mikla, all dragged through Rose’s own Houston heat and private hell. She writes, records, mixes, and directs the entire affair herself, building songs that feel glossy, unstable, wounded, and ready to throw a drink at the mirror. Я ненавижу себя moves between Russian and English as Rose calls herself ugly, rejects advice, declares therapy useless, reaches for alcohol as medicine, and circles the same brutal thought until it becomes a chorus: “Ya Nenavizyu Sebya.” The title translates to “I Hate Myself,” and the track treats that phrase with the blunt force of a diary entry written hard enough to tear the page. There’s face paint, jealousy, body disgust, and the desperate wish to love herself again, all carried by stacked synthesizers and vocals that cut through the arrangement with theatrical ache. The Russian lyrics give somemagicalshit a serrated emotional edge, bending the song’s pain into something harsher, stranger, and more intimate than plain English confession could manage alone. Rose’s voice moves from sneer to exposed nerve without getting coy about the damage, while the music keeps enough pop instinct to make the misery stick in your teeth. “The goal from the beginning was to create something atmospheric and emotionally intense while incorporating the beauty and emotion of the Russian language into alternative electronic music,” says Rose. “That mission hasn’t changed. It’s only getting louder.” The video for Я ненавижу себя, directed by Jorge Delgado, turns self-loathing into a public spectacle with a weird grin taped to its face. Rose performs with live-wire force while an audience watches from behind paper bag masks, reflecting the song’s shame. The clip has the charge of a basement show, a breakdown, and a prank pulled on the bad voice in your head all at once. “This is a song about suffering with self-hatred, making this video was a dream come true for me and I hope that you all enjoy it! It is slightly humorous as well as serious,” says Rose. Watch below: Houston’s alternative scene has already been getting the message, with short tours, out-of-town dates, and new material pushing the project beyond its original bedroom-bunker beginnings. With Re:Mission now behind it, somemagicalshit’s forthcoming full-length looks set to deliver a very stylish nervous breakdown with teeth. Catch somemagicalshit on the road in the America South this summer! June 5, 2026 The Crypt, New Orleans, LA w/ Blood Lovely, Phoenix Phantasma July 10, 2026 The Mix, San Antonio, TX w/ Shelly Webster + more TBA August 28, 2026 Crow Bar (Raven Room), Houston, TX w/ In The Shadows, Andrako, DJ Whisperwish Discover more from Re:Mission Entertainment here, and check out their official Bandcamp page here. items.body: Kurs Murder (P. 1) Swiss Dark Nights One-man Italian act Kurs has had both its musical aesthetic and a unique approach to LP release locked in from its 2021 debut, and isn’t deviating from that approach the third time out. As with preceding Kurs records, Murder (P. 1) isn’t just a concept record in and of itself but also ships with a graphic novel fleshing that concept out. Lacking said book we can only presume that this is intended as the first volume of an ongoing series of records/books, but you don’t need that larger context in order to appreciate Valerio Rivieccio’s yen for moody and stormy electro-industrial. Kurs remains a project which rewards focused headphone listening rather than club fodder hunting, and the loping rhythmic slither and numbly distorted hums on lead single “Weapon” are a great demonstration of why we’ve been waiting so keenly for Kurs’ next move. The ebb and flow of the track’s build and release is considered and never rushed, building towards churning drums and acidic vocals, but along the way there’s much in the way of satisfying and finely textured programming that’s catnip to the seasoned rivethead. Those moves don’t just take the form of traditionally noisy elements, either; opener “Precinct” gradually expands in scope, pulling back from the minimal, chilly EBM pulse of its first moments into a more cinematic mode framed by horns. As always, Kurs is a project whose roots are easy to spot if one cares to look for them, but Murder (P. 1) never comes up short even in that sort of perspective. The influence Front Line Assembly has on Kurs, which has always been detectable in the corners of the preceding records, becomes more apparent on a number of pieces here, as on the Leeb-esque chorus of “Murder” and on the galloping programming of “Basement” which treads the line between martial bombast and pure clattering chaos. Lifts like that don’t necessarily hit the most overt aesthetic or musical cues other bands have taken from FLA, though, and as with preceding LPs Muter and Dreamer so much work has gone into building up Kurs’ own world of sound and atmosphere that these moments (or the occasional parallel with mid-period Haujobb) feel like tips of the hat and never overt coattail riding. The imagery conjured by Murder (P. 1)‘s titles and lyrics are plenty evocative even sans accompanying text, and it’s easy to build a Deus Ex or Dark City inspired landscape in your mind’s eye as you listen. If that all sounds like nostalgia for cyber-dystopias of the past rather than the one we’re living in, fair enough, but once again Kurs have put so much work into their craft that the histories they’re drawing upon soon fade from the listener’s mind as they enjoy Kurs qua Kurs. Buy it. Murder (P. 1) by Kurs The post Kurs, “Murder (P. 1)” appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items.excerpt: Are perfumes composed? Do they evolve? Polish-Canadian trumpeter and composer Jacques Kuba Séguin says they do, emphatically, with his La Trilogie des Odeurs: Three Works, Three Universes, One Story. items.body:
Are perfumes composed? Do they evolve? Polish-Canadian trumpeter and composer Jacques Kuba Séguin says they do, emphatically, with his La Trilogie des Odeurs: Three Works, Three Universes, One Story.

In presenting an olfactory world via an auditory work of art, there is a sense that Séguin is taking things well beyond just perfume to an entire world of odors. It also suggests an entanglement of the senses, and Séguin pushes this suggestion to the max with this trilogy in three separate albums. For Parfum no. 1, he convenes a jazz quartet with pianist Jean-Michel Pilc, bassist Rémi-Jean Leblanc, drummer Kevin Warren, with vocalist Elizabeth Shepherd sitting in on one tune. Leave the connection of odor to sound to the listener here. Synesthesia—where the stimulation of one sense triggers experiences in another—is a real thing. Pianist Jessica Williams said she saw colors with every note or chord she played.

Of the three Parfum albums, No. 1, 2 and 3, Parfum no. 1 is the starkest—a spare, dry sound that may evoke the smell of desert sage as it rides the Santa Ana winds through the chaparral, picking up molecules of the menthol eucalyptus that flourishes in the riverbeds, the rich aromas of damp earth from which these craggy apparitions writhe.

There is much space here, like that desert landscape that birthed the sage. Melodic simplicity and repetition make the music sound ritualistic in a beautiful way. Elizabeth Shepherd's vocals (invocations?) in French are hushed whisperings on "Je suis là."

The music is expressed with an understated patience, as it was in Miles Davis' Ascenseur pour l'échafaud (Fontana, 1957). It is an inward sound that invites reflection and contemplation.

The three albums as a whole are described as a trilogy of smells celebrating the olfactory memories of our lives. This, in itself, marks out ambitious territory via three distinct albums—Parfum no. 1 utilizing the jazz quartet; Parfum no 2 employing a 17-piece jazz band; and Parfum no. 3 bringing in a symphony orchestra, taking the ambitious aspect off the charts.

The olfactory experiences described, auditorily, on Parfum no. 1 are subtle, whiffs of mixed fragrances. Parfum no. 2, the big band set, brings in a riot of bright smells, with brassy primary colors underlain by understated pastel scents and rainbow swirls of harmonic whirlpoolings.

The final chapter, Parfum no. 3 enfolds the jazz quartet with L'Orchestre Symphonique de Trois-Rivières, led by Alain Trudel. Séguin speaks of: "Base notes, or earth notes...the essence of the perfume, the part that clings to the skin and remains imprinted in objects as well as in the soul." While the first chapter of this trilogy speaks to a simplicity of expression and the elementary, youthful experience of the fragrance, Parfum no. 3 takes that early introduction into the complexities of understanding born of time and wisdom into a richer and more complex landscape.

Track Listing: CD 1: La danse du hasard; Promesse de souvenirs; Rencontre au berceau; Je suis là; Éphémère; Candeur. CD 2: La danse du hasard et des dangers; 26 printemps; Paysage pour Muniak; 40 is the new 30; Gratitude. CD 3: How we start again; Il n'y a pas de hasard; Fugue avec Anaïs (à Métis); Entre l'exil et l'insomnie - partie I L'exil; In coelum; Entre l'exil et l'insomnie - partie II L'insomnie; le cortège des fragrances - Les aléas de Mme P.

Personnel: Jacques Kuba Seguin (trumpet), Jean-Michel Pilc (piano), Rémi-Jean Leblanc (bass), Kevin Warren (drums). Additional: Elizabeth Shepherd (vocals). CD 2: L'orchestre de Nationale de Jazz de Montreal. CD 3: Orchestre des Trois Rivieres.

items.excerpt: Rightfully described as a thinking (wo)man's jazz musician, trumpeter-composer-bandleader Steven Bernstein makes deeply cerebral music no matter whether with his own ensembles such as Sexmob and Millennial Territory Orchestra or in heady collaborations with other artists such Jacob Fred Jazz Odyssey.
items.body:
Rightfully described as a thinking (wo)man's jazz musician, trumpeter-composer-bandleader Steven Bernstein makes deeply cerebral music no matter whether with his own ensembles such as Sexmob and Millennial Territory Orchestra or in heady collaborations with other artists such Jacob Fred Jazz Odyssey (see Race Riot Suite (Royal Potato Family, 2011)).

In fact, the products of his imagination resound with such visceral force that those creations render an impact comparable to his membership in Levon Helm's Midnight Ramble Band (or MTO's tribute to Sly Stone). ResoNation Trio and Ultra Resonance, are similarly charged, the former a forward-thinking yet traditionalist-leaning project for which Bernstein recruited the estimable rhythm section of bassist Scott Colley and drummer Nasheet Waits, the latter is a reimagining of that threesome's music overseen by pedigreed engineer and producer Scotty Hard (a long-time collaborator of visionaries unto themselves, Medeski Martin & Wood).

The former is as skeletal as the latter is dense. Yet the two recordings, distinctly different in concept and execution, are nevertheless inextricably linked. Each, in its own way, is a thought-provoking piece, with the respective virtues redolent when played separately or together in sequence, either in the configuration of the single CD or the double vinyl package.

The abstract likes of Bernstein-Colley-Waits' "Turf" benefit as much from the space in the arrangement as the linear progression the three pursue in "Pettiford." Meanwhile, corresponding titles of the companion piece, such as "Rubidium," function similarly, gateways into more or less otherworldly realms.

It is not necessary to listen to Ultra Resonance on headphones to appreciate its aura. Still, that method can reveal more of the multiple layers in the recordings. And, in its own way, that method also proves to be comparatively applicable to the acoustic music: the patient and probing human three-way human interactions that comprise "Woodstock," for instance, radiate both the physical and mental effort involved in the musicianship.

Hard's deeply insistent reformulation of the music through the use of keyboards, various other instruments and percussion, in combination with Jeremy Gustin's varied rhythm devices, emits a presence as haunting as that in the spacious interplay of the ResoNation Trio. Selections from the latter like the one non-original, the blues of "Sitting On Top of the World," resound with comparable levels of mental acumen infused with technical expertise.

A comparatively spooky atmosphere thus pervades most of this seventy-six minutes, even as it is presented in cuts of mostly 3 to 5 minute duration. With its infectious lively cheer, the penultimate track by the trumpeter, bassist and drummer, titled "South," may be the exception to the rule.

Accordingly, the sounds from the three-man ensemble flicker in and out of the well-defined, but dark audio mix during "Argon." And, without ever going on too long to become monotonous, there are just enough similar turns of melody to render more pronounced the heavily rhythmic likes of "Titano." In the end, the overall pacing is that of a well-sequenced live set, without an overabundance of aural esoterica.

It is thus indicative of the seamless yet malleable nature of ResoNation Trio and Ultra Resonance that various elements from each can be interwoven with the other. Reprogramming the CD tracks or alternating the four sides of vinyl extends both the accessibility and the durability of Steven Bernstein and company's eccentric musical orthodoxy.

Track Listing: Turf; Pettiford; Two Shakes; Woodstock; August 3; West; Mammoth; Question; South; Sitting on Top of the World; Argon; Erbium; Chromium; Vibranium; Rubidium; Titano; Radon; Niobium.

Personnel: Steven Bernstein (trumpet, G-trumpet, flugelhorn, EVI), Scott Colley (bass), Nasheet Waits (drums), Scotty Hard (organ, Hammond B3, electronics, percussion), Jeremy Gustin (drums, percussion).

items.excerpt: Larry McCray's Heartbreak City, released on Keeping the Blues Alive Records, is steeped in grit, anguish, resilience and hard-won joy. The album reflects the life of a working-class blues man who sharpened his craft in the clubs of Saginaw after shifts on the General Motors assembly line, before touring nationally and eventually across Europe with Albert Collins.
items.body:
Larry McCray's Heartbreak City, released on Keeping the Blues Alive Records, is steeped in grit, anguish, resilience and hard-won joy. The album reflects the life of a working-class blues man who sharpened his craft in the clubs of Saginaw after shifts on the General Motors assembly line, before touring nationally and eventually across Europe with Albert Collins. Every track carries the emotional weight of decades spent earning success the hard way, drawing deeply from McCray's Arkansas roots while sounding fully grounded in the modern blues tradition.

"Try to Be a Good Man," co-written by McCray, serves as both introduction and mission statement. Riding a chugging roadhouse groove—with a bright, punctuating all-star horn section featuring Dan Fornero, Wayne Bergeron, Andy Martin and Sal Lozano—the song doubles as advice for younger men navigating relationships. McCray's baritone, earthy, warm and unforced, anchors lines such as: "Give her all the love you can and do your best to understand." His guitar work is concise and expressive, delivering sharp, brittle, conversational bends that echo the influence of Little Milton without slipping into imitation.

The title track provides the album's emotional center. Built on a deep blues-rock pocket shaped by the modern production style associated with producers Joe Bonamassa and Josh Smith, "Heartbreak City" unfolds with the restless momentum of an open highway. McCray's stinging guitar lines recall Albert King, while his vocal phrasing again nods to Milton. The song captures the album's defining theme: a man worn down by loss, disappointment and the daily grind, yet still unwilling to surrender. It is weary and determined at the same time, balancing vulnerability with quiet resolve.

On "Everything Falls on Me," McCray channels his frustration through a mid-tempo blues-rock groove shaped by Bo Diddley-style syncopation and terse, declarative guitar figures reminiscent of Chuck Berry. Its lyrics about carrying everyone else's burdens strike a familiar chord without lapsing into self-pity. "When it comes to disaster, Red Cross got nothin' on me / I've cleaned up more messes than the human eye can see / Be it friend or family or someone I just met / They only hit me up for something, anything they can get."

McCray's songwriting strengths surface again in "Bye Bye Blues," co-written with Charlie Walmsley and nominated for Song of the Year at the 2026 Blues Music Awards. Built around the line, "When I said hello to you, I said goodbye to the blues," the song balances classic blues sentiment with understated optimism and demonstrates McCray's ability to write memorable, emotionally direct material.

Throughout Heartbreak City, McCray honors the artists who shaped him while remaining unmistakably himself. Positioned somewhere between Albert King's fire and Little Milton's silky soulfulness, he delivers performances defined by warmth, grit and emotional clarity. In an era still searching for towering modern blues voices, McCray makes a compelling case for his place near the top of the genre's current generation.

Track Listing: Try To Be A Good Man; Heartbreak City; Bye Bye Blues; Bright Side; Everything Falls On Me; I Know What I Have Done; Keep On Loving My Baby; Hangman; Stop Your Crying; Crazy World.

Personnel: Larry McCray (guitar, electric), Joe Bonamassa (guitar), Josh Smith (guitar), Reese Wynans (keyboards), Calvin Turner (bass), Lemar Carter (drums), Kirk Fletcher (guitar), Jade Macrae (vocals), Dannielle De Andrea (vocals), Dan Fornero (trumpet/flugelhorn), Wayne Bergeron (trumpet/flugelhorn), Andy Martin (trombone/bass trombone), Sal Lozano (saxophone/baritone saxophone/flutes).

items.excerpt: Evidence lives up to its title very well. A lot of music in this fairly short album that makes itself heard with surprising simplicity. EVIDENCE is a quartet: reeds, trombone, cello and drums. An unusual formation, but one that recalls Henry Threadgill's Zooid from 2015 onwards.
items.body:
Evidence lives up to its title very well. A lot of music in this fairly short album that makes itself heard with surprising simplicity.

EVIDENCE is a quartet: reeds, trombone, cello and drums. An unusual formation, but one that recalls Henry Threadgill's Zooid from 2015 onwards (without the guitar): In For A Penny, In For A Pound (Pi Recordings, 2015) and Poof. Sol Léna-Schroll (alto saxophone and clarinet) is Threadgill, Jørgen Bjelkerud (trombone) is Jose Davila, Joel Ring that of Christopher Hoffman, and Trym Saugstad Karlsen (drums) is Elliot Humberto Kavee.

The comparison goes no further. For here the music takes flight. The absence of piano and bass is turned to advantage in airy compositions and improvisations, whereas with Threadgill, drums and tuba (which Davila also plays) often take it upon themselves to bring everyone back down to earth. It is a feat of Karlsen's to breathe pulses that propel the music into the air.

Léna-Schroll and Bjelkerud are fellow members of Orchestra for Jazz Composers in Oslo / Orkesteret for Jazzkomponister Oslo (OJKOS) and L'Autre Collectif/Det Andre Kollektivet, a compelling initiative funded by France and Norway since 2019, where the innovative aspects of jazz and sometimes contemporary music are explored, and from which the label Autres Records was born.

The compositions and arrangements are precise and tightly structured. From them emerge improvisations in which the saxophone and trombone interlock in virtuosic spirals ("Mad Blue"). Freed from any earthly support, improvisation breaks free harmonically from the theme, while maintaining its formal rigour.

The brisk compositions would readily be described as bop in other circumstances, with perhaps a welcome Braxtonian touch. In particular, Léna-Schroll delivers a highly inspired solo in "Infinite Loop." The quieter pieces showcase the timbral contrasts, exemplified by an exquisite dialogue between Ring and Bjelkerud in "Infinite Fase."

This is an album of very high calibre with a great deal of substance. The lively and more measured pieces follow one another in a way that gives the album a fine balance. This beautiful, intelligent album is a breath of fresh air, an invitation to freedom, the opening of morning windows, and a day filled with positive energy.

Track Listing: Mad Blue; Infinite Down (#3); Band Music; Choral; Infinite Loop (#1); Infinite Fase (#2).

Personnel: Jørgen Bjelkerud (trombone), Sol Léna-Schroll (alto saxophone, clarinet), Trym Saugstad Karlsen (drums), Joel Ring (cello).

Title: Evidence | Year Released: 2026 | Record Label: Autres Records

items.excerpt: The fourteen-member Hot House West Swing Orchestra, enabled by Salt Lake City, Utah's nonprofit Hot House West, makes its recorded debut with Joy in Rhythm, Vol. 1, an array of eleven danceable songs, most of which were popular during the Swing Era's golden age in the 1930s and '40s.
items.body:
The fourteen-member Hot House West Swing Orchestra, enabled by Salt Lake City, Utah's nonprofit Hot House West, makes its recorded debut with Joy in Rhythm, Vol. 1, an array of eleven danceable songs, most of which were popular during the Swing Era's golden age in the 1930s and '40s.

This is an album especially designed for dancing; it even includes a booklet that teaches the listener a number of simple dance moves tailored for beginners. In spite of the fact that there are several cursory solos along the way (the longest by violinist Curtis Woodbury), this is not a jazz album per se but one that borrows the rhythms of jazz—most notably swing—to press home its danceable message.

As a guide for dancers, Joy in Rhythm works fairly well. One can imagine a dance floor filled with men and women who are grooving to the music. Remove dancing from the equation, however, and the album reveals a number of flaws, not the least of which is the many liberties taken with the character and tempo of the original compositions—some or even all of which were no doubt deemed necessary to make the finished product more accessible to dancers.

The orchestra's vocalists, Hayley Kirkland and Nathan Royal (who doubles on lead guitar and whistling), are at least on a par with many Swing Era band singers, which can be taken as rather faint praise. As for the orchestra, in terms of power and consonance, it is somewhere below the norm when compared to working professional ensembles, which the Hot House West orchestra does not claim to be. To verify that impression, one need do no more than listen to the closing number, Count Basie's classic "One O'Clock Jump." Case closed.

As no one is likely to amass much wealth performing with this group, it is assuredly a labor of love. And that is perhaps how it should be appraised—as a heartfelt summons to dancers and would-be dancers to leave the couch, head for a ballroom and immerse themselves in the irrepressible Joy of Rhythm.

Track Listing: Dark Eyes; Honeysuckle Rose; I'm Gonna Sit Right Down (And Write Myself a Letter); On the Sunny Side of the Street; Katusha; Grand Terrace Rhythm; I've Got Spurs (That Jingle, Jangle, Jingle); Hit That Jive Jack; A Mellow Bit of Rhythm; Them There Eyes; One O'clock Jump.

Personnel: Hot House West (band/ensemble/orchestra), David Ian Baker (bass), Matt Vashlishan (alto saxophone), Josiah Boornazian (saxophone), Brian Woodbury (trombone), Austie Robinson (trumpet), Tom Young (trumpet), Curtis Woodbury (violin), Nathan Royal (guitar, vocals), Hayley Kirkland (vocals), Celeste Robinson (trumpet), James Martak (guitar), Taku Ishikawa (drums), Jacob Ward (drums), Alex Thomson (saxophone), Derek Crane (baritone saxophone), Daniel Burt (trombone).

items.body:
Taylor Swift has announced an original song, ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’, that's set to be featured in the original soundtrack for the upcoming film Toy Story 5. The track was written with longtime collaborator Jack Antonoff and is set to arrive on 5 June, ahead of the film’s worldwide release on 19 June.

‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ marks Taylor’s return to her country roots and was inspired by everyone's favourite cowgirl, Jessie. According to Taylor, she wrote the track after getting an early look at the upcoming film, sharing that the story immediately resonated with her.

Toy Story 5 director Andrew Stanton also praised the song, highlighting Taylor’s connection to Jessie and the way she understood the character’s emotional journey. He described the track as one that feels deeply connected to the world of Toy Story, as though it had always belonged there.

Taylor first teased the announcement with mysterious and playful billboards that were spotted in Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas, San Francisco, Toronto, Mexico City, and London. Each board featured the letters "TS" in the iconic Toy Story font, alongside a Toy Story-themed countdown on her website, following days of fan speculation surrounding her involvement in the film.

After the countdown ended, she finally revealed the surprise on her social media platforms with the caption:

It’s a Toy Story. You knew it! My new original song 'I Knew It, I Knew You' for Disney and Pixar’s Toy Story 5 will be yours on June 5th. I’ve always dreamed of getting to write for these characters who I’ve adored since I was a 5-year-old kid watching the first Toy Story movie. I fell instantly in love with Toy Story 5 when I was lucky enough to see it in its early stages, and I wrote this song as soon as I got home from the screening. Sometimes you just know, right?

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Taylor Swift (@taylorswift)

Toy Story 5 will bring back Woody, Buzz, and Jessie, as the film sees the toys facing a new challenge in the form of children’s growing attachment to electronics. The film will also feature Randy Newman’s returning score.

With both the song and film arriving this June, fans of Taylor Swift and the beloved Toy Story 5 franchise have plenty to look forward to. Blending Swift's heartfelt songwriting with the emotional storytelling that has defined the Toy Story series for decades, ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ is shaping up to be a memorable addition to the film's soundtrack and a fitting companion to Jessie’s next chapter.

items.body:
FIFTY FIFTY embrace flaws and encourage self-discovery on their bold and reflective EP, Imperfect-I’mperfect. The six-track record sees the quartet explore their unique identities and use their artistry to transcend insecurity and instil confidence in themselves and fans.

Life is an unpredictable path that hurls all kinds of situations at us at any time. The EP reinforces the message that perfection is not the ultimate goal. Each song adds a piece to the message that it's impossible to be happy and positive all the time, moments of sorrow and pain aren't weakness, but showcase strength in the ability to be vulnerable. The group first gave fans a glimpse into the record with the pre-release single 'STARSTRUCK'. It was a sonic pivot for the group as they began to build a genre-blurring soundscape with the track's futuristic and electronic music elements. Fusing glowing synth melodies with distorted vocals, the track exudes a retro-cyberpunk style.

At the core of the album lies the focus track 'Like A Bubble'. Much like the title, it talks about shedding the weight of societal expectations and floating through life. The song lies on a fluttery melody and buoyant rhythm that oozes with playful charm and confidence as it encourages listeners to love themselves just as they are, without worrying about conforming. The music video that accompanies the track captures the sense of childlike wonder that comes with being carefree, infusing animated elements that make it feel like an otherworldly dreamscape.

The album takes a wistful turn with the delicate melodies of 'Took It Too Far', which follows the push and pull of a toxic relationship that you can't quite walk away from. 'Genie Magic' picks up the groove once again with its explosive energy and bright chiming synths, celebrating the blissful surprises that romance can bring.

Zeroing in on authenticity and raw honesty, 'PERFECT' blends dreamy R&B textures with subtle retro influences, capturing the thrill of first love through a heartfelt yet confident confession. The record comes to a close with the full and layered musical arrangements on 'Carry On', which instils a sense of hope for the journey ahead with its bright soaring melodies.

Through its mix of dynamic pop tracks and reflective moments, Imperfect-I’mperfect reinforces FIFTY FIFTY’s status as one of pop’s most promising rising acts. Balancing vulnerability with self-assurance, the EP transforms moments of doubt, heartbreak, and uncertainty into a powerful message of self-acceptance, showcasing the group's growing artistic confidence and emotional depth.

items.body:
Get ready to feel the heat, passion, and rush of a charged summer romance as LIL LEAGUE from EXILE TRIBE teams up with NEX and AA from rising Thai pop group BUS because of you i shine. 'LOCA' is also set to claim its spot on LIL LEAGUE from EXILE TRIBE's upcoming double A-side single release.

Translating to crazy in English, 'LOCA' is centred around an alluring woman with fiery and irresistible qualities, whisking listeners into the vibrant hues of a tropical sunset. The track marks a milestone moment for the group as it's their first collaborative track. The bilingual track predominantly features English lyrics, with NEX and AA delivering seamless Japanese vocals, marking an exchange of culture and musical styles.

The addictive rhythm of the track melts into the synth-driven melodies, creating a seductive ensemble that radiates not just the heat of romance but the warm embrace of a summery island escapade. The music video perfectly sets the scene of the track as it was filmed on the beautiful sandy beaches of Pattaya, Thailand.

A mysterious woman dressed in red draws the attention of LIL LEAGUE from EXILE TRIBE members as she walks along the shore, as they try to woo her by describing her effortless glow. As the video unfolds, the focus also shifts to include their new friendships as they enjoy their time on the island. They meet NEX and AA, who work at a seaside café, and have fun together under the Thai sun.

Beyond just a collaboration, 'LOCA' highlights the evolving sound and cross-cultural future of Asian pop. Bringing together Japanese and Thai musical influences, multilingual vocals, and the chemistry between the artists, the track serves as a vibrant celebration of cultural exchange while showcasing the limitless possibilities of music that transcends borders.

items.body:
SHINee transcends the confines of genre and reality with the otherworldly allure of their sixth mini album, Atmos. The six-track album is a testament to the group's growth and the evolution of their sonic individuality.

Each track on the record is a blend of a spectrum of genres, reinforcing the group's versatility. As they incorporate styles like electronic pop, funk, R&B, and dance music, fusing them with their evocative lyricism and lush production, they unveil a new alter ego in their artistry, one that preserves their signature sound while encouraging experimentation through each song on the tracklist.

At the heart of the album lies the title track 'Atmos', which presents a heavy synth-driven melody fuelled by addictive house-style rhythms to truly create a dreamlike soundscape. The song is a quiet documentation of the euphoria that comes with spending time with that special person. Weaving the meaningful verses with the diverse musicality, the track is a quiet depiction of the ultimate form of love, strong enough to grant peace.

The music video aligns with an otherworldly concept, toggling between two realities. With one set in the dark and gloomy background of the thick darkness of late nights in the city, walking through foggy tunnels to find a refreshing countryside where the sun never seems to set. It follows the idea of the butterfly effect as each member crosses paths, stumbling across something each of the other characters loses along the way, like a pair of tangled earbuds or a pair of silver-framed glasses.

SHINee traverses the myriad genres with each track, beginning with 'HOURS', which drips with addictive disco and funk energy perfect to get your groove on, flowing seamlessly into the raw and gritty grunge, alternative rock beat of 'Possibility'. Pivoting towards a more delicate, melodious sound, the music floats into the ethereal electronic-pop sound of 'Anti Believer' and the relaxed R&B-pop groove of 'Still Raining'. The mini album closes on a high note with the glowing radiance of positivity on 'Thousand Miles Away', urging fans to forge their own path to a brighter future.

With Atmos, SHINee once again prove why they remain one of K-pop's most innovative and enduring acts. Blending genre-defying musicality with immersive storytelling and dreamlike visuals, the mini album captures the group's willingness to evolve while staying true to the artistry and emotional depth that have defined their legacy for years.

items.body:
Following a monumental 20 year career, T.O.P gives back to fans who have supported him throughout his journey with a free fan meeting event. Taking place on 9 July at the Pia Arena MM in Yokohama, the venue capacity makes it possible for 10,000 to join and catch their favourite idol live on stage.

Earlier this year, T.O.P announced that he could not be joining G-DRAGON, Taeyang, and Daesung for the highly anticipated festivities as part of BIGBANG's 20th anniversary. While he continues to forge his own path, he thanks fans for their support, despite his decision to continue on as a solo artist. "The fan meet and greet is a performance that T.O.P planned as a gift to the fans who have shown him steady love and support," Topspot Pictures comments.

As he marks two decades in the industry, the fan meeting serves as both a celebration of T.O.P’s remarkable journey and a heartfelt thank-you to the fans who have stood by him through every chapter of his career. With 10,000 fans set to gather in the arena, the special event promises to be an emotional and memorable occasion, bringing artist and fans together to celebrate 20 years of music, growth, and shared memories.

Spotlighting outstanding music and achievements from some of the industry's biggest names is what the MUSIC AWARDS JAPAN 2026 is all about. But no celebration is complete without the electrifying energy of live music, and this year's lineup of performers is set to keep the crowd on their feet. With an exciting roster of artists taking the stage, the second edition of the awards promises to be an unforgettable and iconic spectacle.

With a mix of J-pop heavyweights, K-pop legends and western trailblazers creating an all star lineup of performers, the ceremony is shaping up to be packed with explosive energy and live renditions of hit tracks.

Kicking off the bill are some of J-pop’s fiery frontrunners, with the reverberating rhythms of Kenshi Yonezu alongside the groovy, genre-blending sounds of Fujii Kaze and the power-packed energy of rising girl group HANA. Representing K-pop on the regional stage is MISAMO, the sub unit from legendary girl group TWICE comprising members Momo, Sana, and Mina.

Pledging to champion music regardless of language or borders, Sam Smith is set to bring his award winning melodies and bold expressive performance to the stage. The lineup also features CHANMINA, globally acclaimed rock band sakanaction, shoegaze-influenced duo Hitsujibungaku, and veteran live favourites Tokyo Ska Paradise Orchestra, who will be joined by special guests AiNA THE END, TAKUMA of 10-FEET, and LiSA.

With more performers set to be announced before the Grand Ceremony on 13 June, keep your eyes peeled for information on the official MAJ website.

items.body: By Hrayr Attarian English saxophonist Cath Roberts is an innovative improviser and composer, a graphic artist, organizer, and educator. Roberts’ frequent collaborator and compatriot, bassist Olie Brice, is equally imaginative as his music blurs the line between pre-written and spontaneously created. The pair shares sublime camaraderie, and their professional relationship enhances the brilliance of their individual expressions. All this is fully displayed on their 2026 duo release the provocative Setpieces. The album starts on a riotous note with “Tensile”. Roberts’ fiery refrains spar with Brice’s angular, con arco lines. The delightfully dissonant dialogue seamlessly goes from a passionate, extroverted repartee to parallel introspective musings. Robert’s reverberating baritone complements Brice’s darkly hued bass as their respective improvisations elegantly waver between converging and going their separate ways. This stimulating conversation continues on “Cascades”. Both Roberts and Brice, individually and together, channel more boppish sensibilities without limiting the freedom of their performances. Roberts’ alto has an incandescent, lyrical edge, while Brice creates a dynamic framework with his resonant tones. He plays increasingly complex melodic fragments, to which Roberts responds with agile, muscular phrases. The two musicians mirror one another with clever and inventive ways to make their duets more than the addition of two separate solos. On the melancholic “Anthills”, for instance, Roberts’ pops match Brice’s plucked note s while the saxophonist’s pensive undulations complement the bassist’s dramatic drones. The track grows more wistful as it progresses to its conclusion, and the captivating tension keeps the mood expectant. The poetic sense and intriguing ambiance crystallize on “Shadow Puppets”. Both musicians echo each other with long, mournful soliloquies. Then, as the tune evolves, Roberts’ elegiac extemporization weaves a complex path through Brice’s intricate rhythmic tapestry. The discourse is laced with mysticism, especially as Brice’s dark, percussive passages intermix with Roberts’ warm, yearning ones. This stimulating work showcases the imaginative creativity of two improvisational masters. It is also a perfect example of a sublime balance between individualism and collaborative teamwork. The result is one of the best releases of 2026 so far. Setpieces by Cath Roberts & Olie Brice Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items.body:
Label: Artwork Records, 2026

Personnel - Lakecia Benjamin: alto saxophone; Oscar Perez: piano; Miki Hayama: piano; Elias Bailey: acoustic bass; Jonathan Barber: drums + Guests - Terence Blanchard: trumpet (#1,2); Chief Xian aTunde Adjuah: trumpet (#4); Sean Jones: trumpet (#3,6); Chris Potter: tenor saxophone (#6,8); Jeff Tain Watts: drums (#6); Hiromi: piano (#8,9); Tarriona “Tank” Ball: vocals, spoken word (#7); Bilal: vocals (#10); Kassa Overall: vocals (#10)






















































American saxophonist, composer, and bandleader Lakecia Benjamin responds to the present times and the world around her with We Dream, her sixth album as a leader. Determined to serve as a bright light in dark times, Benjamin expands her soulful musical language—venturing beyond the influence of the Coltranes here—with renewed purpose and the support of an impressive roster of guest artists.

“First Light” plunges into an atmospheric jazz ambiance, gradually brought to a simmer through spoken word and the aching trumpet cries of Terence Blanchard. The opening piece flows seamlessly into “Beyond the Dawn”, which paints a spiritual 3/4 modal landscape elevated by terrifically articulated solos from Benjamin and Blanchard, while drummer Jonathan Barber reinforces the track’s sweeping élan with expressive mallet work.

Exploring themes of isolation and endurance, “My Only” carries a modern jazz-hop sensibility enriched by shifting tempos and a strong contribution from trumpeter Sean Jones. “Mi Gente”, promoting collective unity, features another commanding trumpet voice: Chief Xian aTunde Adjuah, formerly known as Christian Scott. What begins with a soft R&B touch soon blossoms into a glorious Latin-infused section filled with exuberant unisons and swinging momentum.

Hip-hop and R&B are embedded in the DNA of the title track, which features spoken word by New Orleans poet Tarriona ‘Tank’ Ball. This fusion of styles remains vibrant on “Right Now”, where progressive soul singer Bilal and drummer-producer Kassa Overall join forces. Benjamin delivers a forceful, twangy solo here, infused with wah-wah effects and raw energy.

Saxophonist Chris Potter and pianist Hiromi are two especially welcome additions to the lineup. Potter propels “Dream Breaker” into ecstatic post-bop territory alongside Jones and drummer Jeff ‘Tain’ Watts. Hiromi, beyond grooving delightfully on “Hiromi Jam”, also energizes the funk-fusion dimensions of “Flame Keeper”, an eccentric and satisfying romp packed with playful synthesizer flourishes.

While juggling a wide range of genres, Benjamin rarely loses her grip in this contemporary treatise on both creativity and political consciousness. We Dream secures its place—right here and right now—within her increasingly significant body of work.

items.artist: Dominique Cravic et les Primitifs du futur
items.excerpt: Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris café, Dominique Cravic , a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur . Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth. Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic. John Alan Urquhart investigates their crimes. »
items.body: Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris café, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur. Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth. Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I'm guessing here), and musical saw. The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle, just to get the list started. The liner notes point out that "Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove." Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous "Ukulele Lady" from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie's 1971 album Hobo's Lullaby . The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler. A more serious item is "N'oublie pas Gréco" (Don't Forget Gréco") is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gréco, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like "Fumée aux yeux" ("Smoke Gets in Your Eyes"), "Boude pas" ("Take Five"), and "Prive d'amour" ("As Time Goes By"). This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, "The young have fire, but we have light." In its own little corner, Les Crimes du Musette shines bright.

items.excerpt: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with pristine vocals, plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. John Alan Urquhart shares their master class in artistic brevity. »
items.body: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar. Vanishment contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina's clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice. The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette. The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, "Kerosene Madrigal," is a sort of miner's blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of "Imagined Love" reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy "Don't Fault the Stars for Falling" could have been a Dolly Parton tune. "A Grand Expanse" has a more ambitious arrangement. It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun. The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it. Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto's Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.
